svg.title: One Recovery Operation, Distinct Claim Routes
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-06-fund-specific-recovery-responsibilities; chapter number: 11; title: One Recovery Operation, Distinct Claim Routes; subtitle: Coordinate availability research, claimant authority, fund-specific documentation, and payment tracking.; caption: Scott White begins with availability and entitlement. Eric Richardson of Money Making Juggernaut explains bankruptcy research and entity authority. David Wilkerson and Pierce Law Group describe state-funds agreement requirements.; assumptions note: These responsibilities do not establish a reported team size or require separate hires. Unclaimed CEO recommends proving the process repeatedly before delegating it to a virtual assistant.; note: Richardson's bankruptcy guest distinguishes four filings from one payout. A filed or accepted case is not collected revenue, and state-property requirements do not substitute for court requirements.; chart type: org_architecture; center: role: Recovery operator; headcount: Not specified; focus: Match the fund type, money holder, entitled claimant, required agreement, and actual payment status.; spokes: role: Availability and case research; type: Research responsibility; kpi: Availability, existing claims, payment history, and the origin of the funds checked before pursuit, following Scott White and Richardson.; role: Claimant and entity authority; type: Entitlement responsibility; kpi: Authorized corporate signatory identified and entitlement supported, following Richardson's entity-research guidance.; role: Agreement and claim preparation; type: Fund-specific documentation responsibility; kpi: Applicable timing, fee, disclosure, and signature requirements checked, following Wilkerson and Pierce Law Group.; role: Submission and payment tracking; type: Processing responsibility; kpi: Filed, accepted, and paid cases tracked separately, following Richardson's bankruptcy case discussion.
